new_statements.rule_in_words: Pearic words (Pear of Kompong Thom included among the 14 dialects compared) are monosyllables or sesquisyllables: one stressed main syllable, which is the last syllable, optionally preceded by a weakly stressed presyllable with a reduced neutral vowel. Stress therefore falls on the final (main) syllable; there is no polysyllabic stress placement to describe.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Presyllable described as 'weakly stressed'; no secondary stress on longer words discussed.
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress. The presyllable is lost altogether in some Thai Chong dialects (not in Pear of Kompong Thom).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, canonical shape of the lexical word as reconstructed from wordlists (Baradat 1941 for Pear of Kompong Thom); statement is about 'the Pearic word' at branch level, not specific to Pear of Kompong Thom; based on non-phonetic colonial-era transcriptions, no instrumental or fieldwork basis for this language.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog pear1247 = 'Pear of Kompong Thom' (Phnom Tbeng, now Rovieng District, Preah Vihear), the divergent Pearic lect Sidwell 2023 calls KPT and Ferlus/Headley call 'Pear/Péâr de (Kompong) Thom'; Headley's dialect code PK. The quoted statement is Headley's branch-level generalisation over 14 Pearic dialects (Chong, Samre, Somray, Saoch, Suoi and PK), where PK data come only from Baradat's 1941 wordlist. No source describes Pear of Kompong Thom on its own; Bastian's 'Khamen boran' (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description) is only conjecturally this language.

Comparative work on wordlists, not fieldwork on Pear.

3-4 villages in Rovieng District, Preah Vihear (formerly Kampong Thom); 1,670 speakers (Ethnologue 25, 2011 figure); Sidwell 2009 citing Baradat ms calls Pear of Kompong Thom the most divergent Pearic language. No phonology, no stress information.

sources.note: Sec. 1: KPT (Pear of Kompong Thom) is the one Pearic lect not mutually intelligible with the Chongic lects (56-63% shared basic vocabulary); KPT data from Baradat 1941 in non-IPA spelling. Sec. 2 restates Headley's sesquisyllabic template (main syllable C1(C2)V1(F1) preceded by presyllables). No stress statement.
